extracted.intended_audience: aspiring television/sitcom writers and students of comedy writing
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, experience-based guidance on writing television sitcoms, emphasizing character-driven comedy, classic-model study, and structural craft (setups, act breaks, resolutions, ensemble roles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Value fundamentals: storytelling and craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Good story telling and writing craft are always worth learning, even if some of the principles are not in vogue at the moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time in learning timeless storytelling techniques rather than only chasing current trends; core craft applies across eras and formats. (Original text: 'Good story telling and writing craft are always worth learning, even if some of the principles are not in vogue at the moment.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Study classic examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch classic sitcoms to learn how the comedy works in practice: TAXI, CHEERS, FRASIER, THE DICK VAN DYKE SHOW, EVERYBODY LOVES RAYMOND, THE HONEYMOONERS and BILKO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain DVDs/reruns and analyze episodes closely — Levine explicitly recommends getting Taxi DVDs and other classics to see techniques in action. 'If you study TAXI you'll know most of what I'm going to say.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy must come out of the characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch how the comedy comes out of the characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on creating developed, distinct characters whose personalities and choices generate the humor organically rather than inserting jokes that don't arise from character. Study how characters' traits and conflicts create comedic situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use relatable, timeless situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice how relatable most of the situations are even though these shows range in age from ten to forty years old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor basic human decisions and timeless dilemmas (rendered with a comic spin) over topical or trendy premises that may date quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize structure over style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how a story is constructed — its setups, beats, and act architecture — before worrying about surface stylistic flourishes. Structure is the durable part of sitcom craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: How they set up dilemmas
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine how classic shows set up their dilemmas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: what is the inciting situation, how is the problem introduced, and how do early scenes create stakes that propel the episode? Learn typical sitcom setups by reverse-engineering episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: How they build to act breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Study how the writers build to act breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze pacing and scene progression to see how tension/comedy escalates toward commercial breaks—what beats are placed to maximize cliffhanger or payoff at each act end.

rubrics_metrics.name: How they resolve their stories
rubrics_metrics.description: See how classic episodes resolve their stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at payoff and resolution choices: are problems reversed, learned-from, or merely reset? Study the ways a sitcom delivers a satisfying or ironic ending within the three-act structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are there surprises and how they're set up
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether there are surprises; if so, how are they set up?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify misdirection, seeded clues, and small revelations; learn how to plant information earlier so surprises feel earned rather than arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble dynamics and specific roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at the ensemble players. What is each member’s specific role? How do the casts intermingle?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map character functions within the ensemble (straight man, comic foil, eccentric, etc.) and study interaction patterns that create recurring comic rhythms and scene chemistry.
